component.name: Kartoteka
component.summary: Plain-file reference manager and PDF library

description.p: Kartoteka is a reference manager and PDF library for scholarly writing in Typst — a Zotero alternative whose source of truth is plain, git-friendly files. Bibliographic records are Hayagriva YAML on disk; notes are Markdown; nothing is locked in an opaque database.

ul.li: A plain-file library you can edit in a text editor and version with git.
A Typst-ready library.yml regenerated on every change.
Import from Zotero (BetterBibTeX and the Zotero SQLite store).
Full-text search over metadata, notes, annotations, and PDF text.
Bibliography output in SBL and Chicago styles, and annotated Typst.
Acquire references by DOI, arXiv, or ISBN; drop a PDF in to populate an entry.

description.p: 0.7.1 "Firm Spine" — fixes a startup crash that could happen on every launch, not just when opening a library.

ul.li: Fixed a RefCell already borrowed panic that could abort the app on startup for any library with a saved column order, before a window ever appeared.

description.p: 0.7.0 "Whole Volume" — whole-book EPUB search, and the EPUB reader now remembers where you left off.

ul.li: The EPUB reader's search bar has a new "Whole book" toggle: instead of searching only the currently open chapter, it searches every chapter at once and lists each match as a chapter and excerpt you can click to jump straight to.
The EPUB reader now saves your reading position (chapter and scroll position within it) when you close it, and resumes there next time — matching the PDF reader's existing resume behaviour.

description.p: 0.6.1 "Quiet Stack" — fixes a startup crash on opening a library.

ul.li: Fixed a RefCell already borrowed panic that could abort the app on startup when opening a library with a saved column order or a custom field defined.

description.p: 0.6.0 "Deep Stacks" — optional spreadsheet columns, bulk actions, smarter duplicate detection, and a whole-library relations map.

ul.li: The entries spreadsheet can now show optional columns for Tags, Status, and any custom field you've defined, via a new "Columns…" dialog — off by default. Column order and which optional columns are visible are both remembered across sessions.
A "Select multiple" toggle adds a checkbox column and a bulk-action bar for tagging, adding to a collection, or deleting several entries at once.
Custom fields gained a fourth type, Date, with a calendar picker.
"Find duplicates…" now also lists "possible duplicates" caught by title similarity alone, alongside the existing exact DOI/ISBN/title+year matches.
A new whole-library relations map (menu → "Relations map (whole library)…") shows everything connected to everything at once, with a sidebar ranking the most-connected and most-cited entries.
The EPUB reader gained in-chapter search (Ctrl+F) and undo/redo (Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Shift+Z), matching the PDF reader.

description.p: 0.5.1 "Sound Index" — fixes a rare, intermittent search-index rebuild failure, and updates dependencies to close two real denial-of-service security advisories found in a routine dependency audit.
0.5.0 "Cross Reference" — nested collections, drag-to-organize, and a detail pane you edit in place.

ul.li: Text selection (and highlighting/underlining/strikeout) is now line-aware — a straight vertical drag through a paragraph selects each whole in-between line, not just the narrow column under the pointer.
Collections can nest: give a collection a parent and the sidebar shows the resulting tree. Drag an entry from the list straight onto a collection to add it there.
The detail pane is directly editable — Type, Title, Author(s), Year, Publisher, DOI, ISBN, Tags, Status, and Rating all save on Enter or on click-away, no dialog required.
Each entry in the list now shows a small icon when a PDF and/or EPUB is available to open.

description.p: 0.4.0 "Quiet Margin" — a big PDF reader usability pass, and a hang fixed.

ul.li: Continuous scrolling is now the reader's default mode, and the Contents sidebar is user-resizable instead of pinned to the width of the longest chapter title.

Right-click a highlight, underline, strikeout, or note to edit its note or delete it, or right-click blank page space to add a new note — replacing the old "This page" dropdown. A new Notes sidebar lists every note and highlight in the whole document, readable at a glance, not just an on-page icon.
A new "Select text" drag mode copies the covered text to the clipboard instead of creating an annotation. Highlight and search-match colours are also more visible.
Page navigation and zoom moved to a new bottom status bar, freeing the headerbar's title to show the document's own name.

Fixed: opening a PDF, or switching into continuous-scroll mode, could hang the whole window for the document's full render time — page layout is now instant and each page's image renders incrementally afterward.
Fixed: launching Kartoteka while it was already running opened a second window instead of raising the existing one.
Dragging a PDF onto the window to add it now explains a failed drop instead of silently doing nothing.

description.p: 0.3.0 "Loose Leaf" — annotations you can read outside Kartoteka, and proper support for entries with more than one readable attachment.

ul.li: An "Export…" button in the "Annotations…" dialog renders an entry's whole annotation sidecar as a portable Markdown file — one heading per PDF page or EPUB chapter, the highlighted text quoted, then your note below it.

An entry with both a PDF and an EPUB attached now gets a "Read" chooser instead of silently opening whichever the attachments list listed first, and the "Annotations…" dialog's "Go to" buttons correctly route each row to the format that specific annotation actually anchors on.

description.p: 0.2.0 "Marked Folio" — a built-in EPUB reader, and a big round of PDF reader polish.

ul.li: A built-in EPUB reader alongside the existing PDF one — chapter navigation, a table-of-contents jump list, and proper rendering of text, images, and stylesheets via an embedded WebKitGTK view, not just metadata-only import.
EPUB highlighting, with saved highlights reapplied automatically on every chapter load, and EPUB chapter text now indexed for full-text search.

The PDF reader gained underline and strikeout, freestanding notes, a colour picker, an outline/bookmarks panel (now a persistent sidebar), an in-reader search bar, an inline per-page annotation list with editable notes, remembered reading position, continuous scroll, and Zotero-style document page numbering.
A live preview while dragging to highlight/underline/strikeout, and snapshot-based undo/redo for every annotation change (buttons plus Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Shift+Z).

description.p: 0.1.1 "Tidy Shelf" — internal build-hygiene fix, no user-facing changes.

ul.li: Reformatted the codebase with cargo fmt, fixing a long-standing CI format-check failure that had been skipping clippy and tests on every push.
A plain-file library — Hayagriva YAML entries, Markdown notes — that lives in a git repository and stays readable without Kartoteka.
Import from Zotero (BetterBibTeX and the Zotero SQLite store), or acquire references by DOI, arXiv, or ISBN. Drop a PDF or EPUB in and it identifies itself.
A built-in PDF viewer with highlighting and annotation management.
Bibliography output in SBL and Chicago styles, and annotated Typst documents.
Full-text search over metadata, notes, annotations, and PDF text.
Typed relations and a knowledge-graph layer — link entries to people, concepts, and schools of thought, not just to each other.
Sync via git, GitHub, or WebDAV.
